Rashi on Yevamot 35b:13:1.hebrew: מדרבנן ולחומרא - דלמא אתי למישרי חלוצה לכהונה, דלא ידעי דהואי מעוברת:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:13:1.english: By rabbinic [decree] and as a stringency - Lest [people] come to permit a chalutzah to [marry into] the priesthood, since they do not know that she was pregnant.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:14:1.english: This is [why] it teaches "she is disqualified," and [it is] as a stringency - and it does not explicitly teach: "she does not require chalitzah from the brothers."

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:15:1.hebrew: אלא לדידך - דאמרת חליצה מעלייתא היא, לישמעינן הא דאינה צריכה חליצה, ואנא ידענא דאסורה בקרוביו ופסלה מן הכהונה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:15:1.english: Rather, according to you - Since you say [it] is a valid ḥalitza, [the mishna] should have taught us this, that she does not require ḥalitza, and I would know [from that] that she is forbidden to his relatives and it disqualifies her from the priesthood.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:15:2.hebrew: ואיידי דתנא רישא לא פסלה - ולא תנא חליצה, דהתם לא מצי למימר וצריכה חליצה, תנא נמי סיפא פסלה ולא איירי בחליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:15:2.english: And since the first clause taught, "it does not disqualify her" - and did not teach [about] ḥalitzah, because there it could not say "and she requires ḥalitzah," it also taught in the latter clause, "it disqualifies her," and did not discuss ḥalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:16:1.english: [If] the offspring is not viable, he may maintain [her] - [This refers to the mishnah:] One who marries his yevama and she is found to be pregnant.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:18:1.hebrew: היינו דקתני יקיים - דלא מצריך ביאה לאחר שהפילה, ואם בא לגרשה בגט — מגרשה, דאיפטרה לה בביאה קמייתא, וביאת מעוברת שמה ביאה, דקס"ד יקיים דקתני מתני' לאו חובה היא אלא התירא, משום דתנא רישא: אם הולד של קיימא יוציא:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:18:1.english: This is why it teaches: "He may maintain [her]" - For he does not require intercourse after she miscarried, and if he comes to divorce her with a bill of divorce, he may divorce her, since she was exempted [from the levirate bond] by the first intercourse, as intercourse with a pregnant woman is considered [valid] intercourse; for we initially thought [that] "he may maintain [her]" that the Mishnah teaches is not an obligation, but rather a permission, because the first clause taught: "If the offspring is viable, he must send [her] out."

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:18:2.hebrew: דלא סגי בלא"ה - דלא מיפטרה בלא ביאה לאחר שהפילה, דאם לא יחזור ויבעול, לא מצי למפטרה בגט, דאין אדם יכול להוציא את יבמתו בגט אא"כ כנסה תחלה, וביאת מעוברת לאו שמה ביאה. ובחליצה נמי לא אפשר למפטרה, הואיל ומ"מ בא עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:18:2.english: That [it] does not suffice without this - For she is not released without intercourse after she has miscarried, since if he does not go back and have intercourse [with her], he cannot release her with a bill of divorce, for a man cannot send away his yevama with a bill of divorce unless he took her in [through levirate marriage] first, and intercourse with a pregnant woman is not considered [valid] intercourse. And through chalitzah as well it is not possible to release her, since he nevertheless had intercourse with her.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:19:1.hebrew: רצה יוציא - בגט, רצה יקיים מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:19:1.english: If he wishes he may send [her] out - With a bill of divorce, "if he wishes he may maintain [her]" it should have [taught].

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:1:1.hebrew: החולץ הוא מותר בקרובותיה - דלאו חליצה היא, דהא לא בעיא:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:1:1.english: One who performs ḥalitza ... he is permitted to her relatives - For it is not [a valid] ḥalitza, since she did not require [it].

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:1:2.hebrew: קרובותיה וקרוביו - מפרש לקמן במתני' הנך דנאסרות על האיש מחמת אשתו, וקרוביו שנאסרים על האשה מחמת בעלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:1:2.english: Her relatives and his relatives - [It] explains later in the Mishnah those [relatives] who become forbidden to the man on account of his wife, and his relatives who become forbidden to the woman on account of her husband.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:20:1.hebrew: אלא שמא לא יהא ולד של קיימא - ונמצאת זקוקה ליבם, וביאת מעוברת לא שמה ביאה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:20:1.english: Rather, lest the offspring not be viable - And [the rival wife] is found to be bound to the yavam, and intercourse with a pregnant woman is not considered [valid] intercourse.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:2:1.english: If the offspring is not viable - That it was a non-viable infant.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:3:1.english: And they are obligated [to bring] an offering - For he cohabited with a brother's wife not in the context of a mitzvah.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:5:1.english: The child is legitimate - Either way.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:6:1.english: Gemara: She does not require chalitzah from the brothers - For this is a valid chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 35b:7:1.hebrew: שמה חליצה - היכא דהפילה, דאיגלאי מילתא דבת חליצה הואי:
Rashi on Yevamot 35b:7:1.english: It is considered ḥalitza - Where she miscarried, for the matter was revealed [retroactively] that she was subject to ḥalitza.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:10:1.hebrew: תגלי מילתא למפרע לא אמרינן - אע"ג דלקמן (יבמות דף מא:) גבי ספקות, שקידש אחת משתי אחיות, חשבינן לה בת חליצה ויבום כיון דאם יבוא אליהו ויאמר דהא קדיש — לא דמי, דהכא אין זה ספק ראוי להתברר עכשיו, שא"א לידע העתידות; אבל התם א"צ לידע אלא מה שבאותה שעה. וא"ת: לריש לקיש, הכונס יבמתו מעוברת והפילה, אמאי פטור מן הקרבן? כיון דביאת מעוברת לא שמה ביאה, א"כ אשת אח שלא במקום מצוה היא. ואר"י, דאפ"ה לא מחייב, מידי דהוה אקטן שבא על יבמתו גדולה, דאמר לקמן (יבמות דף לט) דתגדלנו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:10:1.english: We do not say that the matter will be revealed retroactively - Even though later (Yevamot 41b), regarding cases of doubt where one betrothed one of two sisters, we consider her subject to ḥalitza and levirate marriage [since the matter can be clarified] if Elijah comes and says that he betrothed this one — it is not comparable; for here, this is not a doubt that is fit to be clarified now, as it is impossible to know future events, whereas there, one only needs to know what [occurred] at that [earlier] time. And if you ask: According to Reish Lakish, when one marries his pregnant yevamah and she miscarries, why is he exempt from the [sin-]offering? Since cohabitation with a pregnant [yevamah] is not considered [valid] cohabitation, if so, she is a brother's wife [in a situation] where there is no mitzvah [of levirate marriage]. And R. Yitzchak says that even so he is not liable, just like a minor who cohabits with his adult yevamah, regarding which [the Gemara] says later (Yevamot 39) that she should raise him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:11:1.hebrew: והא לית ליה - כיון דהפילה לבסוף, אבל בר קיימא לא. א"נ, כשהוא בר קיימא, נפקא לן מ"להקים שם" ומ"לא ימחה" — פרט לזה שאין שמו מחוי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:11:1.english: And this [man] does not have [a child] - Since she miscarried in the end, [this applies,] but [if the fetus is] viable, [it does] not. Alternatively, when it is viable, we derive [his exemption] from "to establish a name" and from "shall not be blotted out" — excluding this [man], whose name is not blotted out.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:11:2.hebrew: וריש לקיש סבר בין אין לו עיין עליו - הואיל ובאותה שעה היה ראוי להתקיים. וא"ת: א"כ, תפטר לשוק בלא חליצה, כמו בזרע פסול דנפקא לן (לעיל יבמות דף כב:) נמי מאין לו; ואמאי נמי אמרינן לקמן דולד אינו פוטר עד שיצא לאויר העולם? ויש לומר: דאמרינן נמי עיין עליו — שלא תחלוץ ולא תנשא כל זמן שעומדת בספק:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:11:2.english: And Reish Lakish holds: "[And] he has no [child]" — inspect him - Since at that time [the fetus] was fit to survive. And if you say: If so, she should be exempted to [marry into] the general public without ḥalitza, just like with disqualified offspring, which we also derive earlier (Yevamot 22b) from "he has no [child]"; and why do we also say later that a fetus does not exempt [her] until it emerges into the air of the world? One can say: We also say "inspect him" — [meaning] that she may neither perform ḥalitza nor marry as long as she stands in doubt.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:19:1.hebrew: רצה יוציא רצה יקיים מיבעיא ליה - והא דקתני לעיל גבי ד' אחין: "ב"ש אומרים יקיימו", ולא קתני "רצו" — משום דהתם ליכא למיטעי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:19:1.english: "If he wishes he may send [her] out, if he wishes he may maintain [her]" — it should have [taught] - And as for that which it teaches earlier regarding [the Mishnah of] Four Brothers: "Beit Shammai say: They may maintain [them]," and it does not teach "if they wish" — [that is] because there, there is no room to err.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:1:1.hebrew: החולץ ליבמתו ונמצאת מעוברת - הא דלא נקט "החולץ למעוברת" כדנקט בגמ', משום דרבותא היא: דאע"ג דלא היה עוברה ניכר בשעת חליצה ונראית חליצה מעולה, אפילו הכי לא פסלה בזמן שהולד של קיימא. ובגמ' נקט נמי "למעוברת" לרבותא — דאע"פ שהוכר עוברה, כיון שהפילה, חליצה מעלייתא הויא. א"נ, נקט "נמצאת" משום סיפא, דהתם לא מצי למיתני "הכונס ליבמתו מעוברת", דא"כ מזיד הוא ולא מיחייב קרבן, דלא שב מידיעתו הוא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:1:1.english: "One who performs ḥalitza with his yevama and she is found [to be] pregnant" - The reason [the Mishna] did not state "One who performs ḥalitza with a pregnant woman" as it states in the Gemara is because it is a novelty: even though her fetus was not noticeable at the time of ḥalitza and it appeared [to be] a valid ḥalitza, even so it does not disqualify her when the offspring is viable. And in the Gemara it also states "with a pregnant woman" as a novelty: even though her fetus was noticeable, since she miscarried, it is a valid ḥalitza. Alternatively, [the Mishna] stated "she is found" because of the latter clause, for there it could not teach "One who marries his pregnant yevama," because if so, he is an intentional transgressor and would not be liable for a sin offering, as he is not [one who] "turns back upon becoming aware" [of an unwitting sin].

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:1:2.hebrew: ונמצאת מעוברת - בחולץ תוך ג' חדשים איירי, דומיא דסיפא דהכונס יבמתו דאיירי תוך ג'; דאי לאחר ג', אמאי חייב קרבן? כיון דרוב נשים עוברן ניכר לשליש, וזו הואיל ולא הוכר עוברה, מאי הוה ליה למיעבד? וכה"ג אמרינן בשבועות (דף יח. ושם): "פרט לאנוס", גבי שלא בשעת וסתה. וא"ת: אם כן, אם אין הולד של קיימא, אמאי אסור בקרובותיה? דתוך שלשה חדשים לאו חליצה היא, דהא תנן לקמן: "היבמה לא תחלוץ ולא תתייבם עד שיהיו לה ג' חדשים", ומפרש בגמ' טעמא: דכיון דאינה עולה ליבום, אינה עולה לחליצה. ואר"י: דנהי דלאו חליצה היא, מ"מ אסור בקרובותיה, כיון דמדאוריי' הויא חליצה. ועוד: דדיעבד, אם חלצה, אפילו מדרבנן אינה צריכה חליצה אחרת; דאמר לקמן: "יבמה שחלצו לה אחין בתוך ג', צריכה להמתין ג' חדשים" — משמע דלא בעיא חליצה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:1:2.english: And she is found to be pregnant - [The Mishnah] is speaking of one who performs ḥalitza within three months [of her husband's death], similar to the latter clause [of the Mishnah], "One who marries his yevama," which speaks of within three [months]. For if [it were speaking of] after three [months], why would he be liable for a [sin-]offering [in the latter clause]? Since the pregnancy of most women is recognizable at a third [of the pregnancy, i.e., three months], and as for this woman, since her pregnancy was not recognizable, what could he have done? And similarly we say in Shevuot (18a and there): "Excluding one who is forced [by circumstances beyond his control]," regarding [cohabiting] not at the time of her expected period. And if you say: If so, if the offspring is not viable, why is he forbidden to her relatives? For within three months it is not a [valid] ḥalitza, as we learned in the Mishnah later: "A yevama may neither perform ḥalitza nor enter into levirate marriage until she has [waited] three months," and the Gemara explains the reason: that since she is not eligible for levirate marriage, she is not eligible for ḥalitza. And R"I says: Granted that it is not [a proper] ḥalitza, nevertheless he is forbidden to her relatives, since by Torah law it is a [valid] ḥalitza. And furthermore, after the fact, if she performed ḥalitza, even by rabbinic law she does not require another ḥalitza, as [the Gemara] states later: "A yevama with whom the brothers performed ḥalitza within three [months] must wait three months" — which implies that she does not require [another] ḥalitza.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:20:1.hebrew: הרי זו לא תנשא צרתה - כ"ש היא שלא תנשא ושלא תבעל, אלא צרתה איצטריך, שלא תאמר תנשא ממה נפשך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:20:1.english: Her rival wife may not marry - All the more so she herself may not marry [another man] and may not have intercourse [with the yavam]; rather, [the baraita] needed [to state the law regarding] her rival wife, so that you would not say she may marry either way.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:22:1.hebrew: כולי עלמא לא פליגי - הא דקאמר לעיל "איתיביה הכונס יבמתו" — להד"מ. וכה"ג איכא בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כד.) גבי "פניו ממוסמסין", ובכמה דוכתין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:22:1.english: Everyone agrees - That which [the Gemara] said above, "He raised an objection: One who marries his yevama" — [that] never happened [i.e., that objection is unfounded]. And similarly there is [such an instance] in the chapter [entitled] Hamapelet (Niddah 24a) regarding "its face is dissolved," and in several [other] places.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:22:2.english: When they disagree, [it is] with regard to ḥalitza - And with regard to intercourse he concedes, so that he will not come to a prohibition.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:6:1.hebrew: צריכה חליצה מן האחין - לאו דוקא מן האחין, דה"ה דלא פקעה זיקת החולץ; אי נמי, מן האחין של מת קאמר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35b:6:1.english: "She requires ḥalitza from the brothers" - [This does] not [mean] specifically from the [other] brothers, for the same law applies that the levirate bond of the one who performed ḥalitza has not been dissolved; alternatively, [it] means from the brothers of the deceased.
